description: Hormone-state module: exactly three per-agent variables (stress_x, sleep_pressure, dopamine_tonic). Tags: [V] verified against the named source by reading it; [D] design default, not claimed to be empirical; [U] unverified or contested. Times are in hours unless the name says otherwise. See docs/hormone_evidence.md.

b_floor.note: stress baseline floor (x units) while asleep and late in the day

b_mood_shift.note: extra floor per unit of a lowered mood-baseline-shift dial (static, not allostatic drift)

A_car.note: awakening-response amplitude; the reported 50-75% rise was not verified

tau_car_h.note: awakening-response peak ~40 min after waking; Stalder et al. 2016 (doi:10.1016/j.psyneuen.2015.10.010) describe a marked rise over the first 30-45 min; 40 min is a [D] choice within that window

tau_s_h.note: phasic stress decay; loosely after a 60-90 min plasma cortisol half-life, itself unverified as a psychological timescale

g_s.note: stress gain per unit threat appraisal

theta_ts.note: threat-sensitivity dial gain on stress increments

g_novelty.note: novelty gain: increment x (1 + g_novelty x surprise)

habituation_power.note: repeat increments scale by 1/(1 + exposures)^power, so they fade within 1-2 exposures

k_controllability.note: threat x (1 + k (0.5 - controllability)); neutral 0.5 when no provider

dys_gain.note: dysregulation dial raises stress gain by (1 + dys_gain x dys)

dys_tau.note: dysregulation dial slows recovery: tau_s x (1 + dys_tau x dys)

rt_bias.note: low reality testing reads threat into arousing events: + rt_bias (1 - reality_testing)(1 - threat) arousal

reactivity_sigma.note: seeded per-agent log-normal spread of stress gain

sleep_dep_reactivity.note: flag: sleep pressure raises stress gain

lambda_p.note: used only with sleep_dep_reactivity: gain x (1 + lambda_p x P)

tau_rise_h.note: Process S rise; two-process model (Daan, Beersma and Borbely 1984, Am J Physiol 246:R161) - number seen only as a software default, original not read

P_start.note: sleep pressure when the module first sees an agent

circadian_peak_hour.note: clock hour of peak circadian sleep propensity before the chronotype offset

chronotype_sd_h.note: seeded per-agent circadian phase offset; not tied to Big Five

wired_override.note: hypothesis flag: high stress at night lengthens sleep onset and lowers sleep efficiency

L_k_min.note: extra latency scale (minutes) for stress above S_wired

S_wired.note: stress readout above which onset slows

latency_spread.note: seeded latency = mean x (1 - spread + 2 spread u)

k_eff.note: sleep efficiency = 1 - k_eff x S at onset (pressure drains slower after a stressed bedtime)

v0.note: prior expectation for a new target

n_open.note: openness raises the prior: V0 = v0 + n_open x openness

kappa_c.note: closeness term in wanting (absorbs the bonding role; no oxytocin variable)

eta.note: tonic dopamine gain per unit prediction error

d_mood_shift.note: mood-baseline-shift dial moves the resting level: D0 = d0 + d_mood_shift x shift

tau_d_h.note: tonic decay toward D0 (hours to days)

gist_weight.note: learning weight of a GIST-attended outcome (FULL 1, NONE 0)

rho_k.note: reward sensitivity rho = 1 + rho_k tanh(D - D0)

initiative_k.note: initiative multiplier on starting interactions: 1 + initiative_k tanh(D - D0)

menu_wanting_weight.note: how much wanting W(person) adds to a talk option in the living-world menu

lambda_T.note: used only with stress_exploration_link: T = T0 (1 + lambda_T S)

leave_margin.note: leaving is considered once the best alternative beats the current group by this margin

leave_h0.note: leaving probability per decision event per unit shortfall beyond the margin (capped at 1)

arousal_load.note: arousal readout weight of recent event load (open attention streams)

load_ref.note: streams at which load counts as full

arousal_form.note: how arousal scales attention capacity; tunnel vision and the inverted U are not established, so off by default

k_mono.note: monotone form: capacity x (1 - k_mono arousal)

lambda_s.note: negative mood impulses scale by (1 + lambda_s S at the event)

beta_d.note: mood baseline offset per unit (D - D0)

beta_s.note: mood baseline offset per unit (S - S0)

S0.note: stress readout counted as neutral for the mood offset

style_S_mild.note: stress readout for the mild style line

style_S_strong.note: stress readout for the strong style line

style_P.note: sleep pressure for the tired style line

first_person_low_mood.note: flag: low mood adds slight first-person emphasis

low_mood.note: mood valence counted as low for that flag

length_bias.note: stress does not shorten speech by default (no verified source for either direction)

style.stress_mild: A little on edge right now: thoughts come less smoothly, with the odd pause or filler ("um", "I mean").
style.stress_strong: Under heavy strain right now: phrasing comes out simpler and more fragmented, with restarts, pauses and fillers.
style.length_neutral: Say as much as you normally would.
style.length_shorter: You tend to say less than usual.
style.length_longer: You tend to ramble a bit more than usual.
style.tired: Very tired right now: flatter in feeling and slower to respond.
style.first_person: Low in mood: you talk about yourself ("I", "me") a little more than usual.
